0.0.n: A brief, casual greeting here; it can also express thanks in other situations.

0.2.n: His family name, placed before his given name in Japanese.

0.3.n: This character belongs to the given name 勇斗, read はやと; it is not a separate word here.

0.4.n: This character completes the given name 勇斗, read はやと; it is not a separate word here.

0.5.n: A polite sentence ending used after his name to introduce himself.

1.0.n: A polite way to address the audience as a group.

1.1.n: The noun form of 気づく, with お added to show respect toward the audience.

1.2.n: Links お気づき to 通り, forming an expression meaning as you have noticed.

1.3.n: After a noun plus の, 通り indicates that something matches what was mentioned.

2.0.n: A neutral, polite way to refer to oneself; the topic particle は is omitted here.

2.2.n: Refers to the hair on his head, rather than body hair.

2.3.n: Marks 髪の毛 as what undergoes the change.

2.4.n: Describes hair clipped very short all over, not necessarily shaved completely bare.

2.5.n: Marks 丸刈り as the resulting state in the pattern を…にする.

2.6.n: Polite past of させていただく, a humble expression presenting his action as something he was allowed to do.

3.0.n: Indicates when this television drama series airs.

3.1.n: Connects 朝 to the following phrase, describing it as a morning series.

3.2.n: Part of 連続テレビ小説, indicating a drama told across successive episodes.

3.3.n: Part of the fixed expression 連続テレビ小説 for a serialized TV drama.

3.4.n: Usually means novel, but in 連続テレビ小説 it refers to a serialized television drama.

3.6.n: The drama's title, which literally means rice ball.

3.8.n: Marks the drama as the setting in which he plays this role.

3.9.n: Short for 高等学校; it modifies 球児 to specify the player's school level.

3.10.n: Commonly used for school-age baseball players, especially high school players.

3.11.n: Marks 高校球児 as the role he plays.

3.12.n: The plain nonpast form of 演じる, used for portraying a character or role.

3.13.n: Introduces the reason for the haircut explained in the next line.

4.0.n: Refers to his head, with the haircut understood to affect its hair.

4.1.n: Marks 頭 as what undergoes the change.

4.2.n: Describes a uniformly very short haircut rather than necessarily a bare scalp.

4.3.n: Marks the resulting hairstyle in the pattern を…にする.

4.4.n: The polite past form of する; with に, it describes changing something into a particular state.

0.tip: Japanese introductions often omit I and simply put です after the speaker's name.

1.tip: お気づきの通り is a respectful way to say as you have noticed.

2.lit: I, my hair into a buzz cut humbly was allowed to make.
2.tip: させていただきました makes the statement humble; it need not imply that someone explicitly gave permission.

3.lit: Because in the morning serialized television drama Omusubi, a high school baseball player I play,
3.tip: ので connects this reason to the haircut statement that follows.

4.lit: My head into a buzz cut I made.
4.tip: The pattern を…にする means to change something into a particular state.
